title: Etale finite-Tor flat models with their termwise geometric pullback
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $l=f_e^*$ for module inverse image, identified with $f_e^{-1}$ through $f_e^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and also write $l$ for its induced derived functor. Let $u\le v$ be integers, and let $M\in D^b_c(Y_e,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[u,v]$, meaning that $\mathcal H^j(M\otimes_A^LN)=0$ for $j\notin[u,v]$ and every degree-zero $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
There exists an integer-indexed cochain complex $V^\bullet$ of $A_Y$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] such that $V^h=0$ for $h\notin[u,v]$, every $V^h$ is flat, and $M\cong Q_Y(V^\bullet)$ in $D(Y_e,A)$, where $Q_W$ is cochain localization. Flat here means exactness of tensoring with that term [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], on either side of the sheafified tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every such $V^\bullet$, both $V^\bullet$ and the termwise pullback $lV^\bullet$ are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]; the latter has flat terms, is zero outside $[u,v]$, and there is an isomorphism
$$lM\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_X(lV^\bullet)$$
in $D(X_e,A)$, obtained by applying $l$ to the chosen representing isomorphism and the exact-functor localization comparison. No local freeness of the terms or finite-type, properness or closed-immersion condition on $f$ is assumed. Zero complexes, empty schemes and $u=v$ are allowed.

Input existence is lem-sf-flat-model, small-etale clause; exactness conversion uses sites-modules.tex Tag 03EP, lemma-tensor-commute-colimits, and Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact; derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor.

proof.text: Apply finiteCoefficient_hasTorAmplitude_iff_flatModel from [lem-sf-flat-model] to the given finite coefficient complex. It supplies V, its support in [a,b], categorical flatness of every term, and the representing isomorphism. Convert categorical flatness to site-flatness using etaleConstantModule_flat_iff from [lem-pur-etale-constant-module-flat]. The realization is exactly etaleSumFlatModuleRealization; no terms or representing isomorphism are changed.

For any complex with the stated flatness and support, realize it degreewise with etaleSumFlatModuleRealization. This functor preserves zero morphisms and zero objects. Its realized complex is strictly bounded above by b, because each degree h>b is zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] to this realized complex. This proves the first K-flatness assertion for every model, not only the model just constructed.

Use [lem-pur-etale-constant-module-flat] backwards on each term. The existing upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat instance, proved in the module of [lem-sfb-etale-flat-geometric-fibers], makes each inverse-image term categorically flat: its geometric stalk is the original stalk at the composite geometric point. Convert back to site-flatness on X. The additive exact inverse-image functor preserves zero objects, hence the support in [a,b]. Apply the bounded-above flat criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] to the realized inverse-image complex. Thus the second K-flatness assertion follows without constructing a general ringed-topos pullback presentation.

Apply the existing definition etaleTorFlatPullbackModelIso to the chosen representing isomorphism e. It is the composite of mapIso e with mapDerivedCategoryFactors at V from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Package this specified isomorphism and the previous four assertions into the required conjunction. No further hypothesis on f is used.
